slides.headline: A sarod maestro and his two sons recorded an album with the Dalai Lama. It won a Grammy.
Ustad Amjad Ali Khan, with sons Amaan and Ayaan Ali Bangash, won the 68th Grammy Award for Best Audio Book, Narration and Storytelling Recording
slides.body: The winning album, 'Meditations: The Reflections of His Holiness the Dalai Lama,' paired the Dalai Lama's spoken reflections with the Khan family's sarod - a classical Indian stringed instrument - across a genre category built for words, not usually music.

slides.headline: The Dalai Lama didn't receive his own Grammy statuette until months after the ceremony.
slides.body: Amjad Ali Khan personally presented the Dalai Lama with his Grammy at his Dharamshala residence in June 2026 - closing the loop on a collaboration that crossed three generations of one Indian musical family and a Tibetan spiritual leader.

slides.eyebrow: Why it matters for Viksit Bharat 2047
slides.headline: A Viksit Bharat's culture travels furthest when it's shared, not just performed.
slides.body: A sarod lineage built over three generations found a global audience by collaborating outward, not performing in isolation - a model for how Indian classical art keeps finding new rooms to fill.
